note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. Saintfield was the only division contested: Herbert Rogers polled 1,903 and John Johnston 924, so Rogers was returned and Johnston was not. The other eighteen divisions were filled without a contest. The Returning Officer's 'Notice of Result of Elections 1964 - County of Down', dated 4 June 1964 and printed in the Irish News of 10 June 1964, p. 2, names the person returned for every division except Newry, where the poll had been countermanded because Mr. F. G. Mulligan (Newry Labour) died between nomination day and polling day; Newry Labour did not renominate (Irish News, 13 June 1964), and the Deputy Returning Officer's notice dated 15 June 1964 declares Thomas Joseph Kelly elected for Newry without a poll (Newry Reporter, 18 June 1964, p. 10; round 2, 7 Nov 2026). The notice prints no party labels, so none are recorded. The poll called for 4 June 1964 between Kelly and F. G. Mulligan (Newry Labour) was countermanded when Mulligan died between nomination day and polling day; Newry Labour did not renominate, and Kelly was declared elected (notice dated 15 June 1964). Addresses printed with the name are not reproduced. Returned unopposed.
